ideas.risks: A hardness result for relaxed halfspaces may miss the exact nonnegative integer zero-threshold class. A positive selector would still leave the upstream hidden-clean bag-generation problem unresolved.
ideas.summary: Study empirical risk minimization over the exact DCHP final class V_{B,T}=sign(sum_j k_j h_j), with k_j nonnegative integers summing to T and sign(0)=1. Try for either a polynomial or FPT selector when T=O(log(1/epsilon)), or a hardness reduction for approximate ERM on arbitrary binary feature bags, including cases with complements/constants.
ideas.title: Exact Sparse-Majority Selector Dichotomy
ideas.why_promising: Iteration 6 isolated this as a concrete bottleneck. It is precise, separable from hidden-clean generation, and a theorem either way would clarify whether the DCHP near miss is only upstream or also computationally blocked.

ideas.risks: A pathological weak learner does not rule out a different controlled learner for the same class. The construction must matter for black-box reductions that are given only the source learner A.
ideas.summary: Construct weak learners satisfying OPT+beta that encode arbitrary sample-dependent bits in tiny or validation-irrelevant regions, forcing huge Range(A), VC, or dual VC while preserving the weak guarantee. Then test whether any generic wrapper can canonicalize, prune, or ignore the junk without additional assumptions.
ideas.title: No-Free-Regularization Weak Learners
ideas.why_promising: This directly probes whether controlled range, compression, or stability can be derived from the atlas source, which is the main missing assumption in the DCHP route.

ideas.risks: Known refutation or CSP algorithms may not give arbitrary signed distribution-free approximation. Strong-side hardness must be improper prediction hardness, not assignment recovery or refutation hardness.
ideas.summary: Instantiate the approximation-gap template with one explicit succinct signed-CSP or refutation class. Define the descriptor domain so it is superpolynomial, keep the RHS/sign as the label, prove or cite a signed/weighted constant-factor approximator, and separately formulate RCN sample-access hardness against arbitrary improper predictors.
ideas.title: Succinct Signed-CSP Approximation Candidate
ideas.why_promising: The solver attempt gives a clean weak-side lemma: constant-factor agnostic approximation implies fixed-slack weak learning. A single candidate passing this checklist could yield a conditional separation.

ideas.risks: Classical decoding hardness is often proper or full-word, not improper PAC prediction. Efficient list decoding or validation handles may accidentally give strong learning.
ideas.summary: Revisit codeword classes only over succinct or exponential coordinate domains. Look for low-radius weighted soft decoders that give weak learning when OPT<gamma, while RCN prediction at eta>gamma is average-case hard for arbitrary improper hypotheses.
ideas.title: Succinct Codeword RCN Separation
ideas.why_promising: The RCN identity converts strong agnostic learning into prediction of the planted codeword. This keeps the negative target aligned with improper PAC rather than nearest-codeword recovery.

ideas.risks: The result may remain only a toy oracle barrier, not an atlas separation. Public witnesses, spike queries, and oracle-handle leakage must be routed explicitly.
ideas.summary: Build a stopped-process random-hidden-target model where f is random on a large domain, labels have RCN noise eta>gamma, and the transcript includes raw samples, selected filters/relabelings, and oracle replies. Prove that before enough mutual information about f accumulates, every smooth target-useful query still has hidden noise at least gamma; public or spike low-OPT queries receive canonical dummy answers.
ideas.title: Stopped-Process Hidden-Target Barrier
ideas.why_promising: This would turn the public-filter and posterior-envelope lemmas into a coherent lower-bound model, clarifying exactly what information a fixed-slack oracle must leak to enable boosting.

ideas.risks: The condition may be nearly as strong as knowing the comparator’s clean/noisy status. Even if a low-noise chunk exists, a separate update or potential argument is needed.
ideas.summary: Search for natural assumptions under which excess over a near-optimal comparator forces a public low-noise chunk: for example Massart/Tsybakov-style posterior tails, calibration of the current predictor, or structured feature partitions. Then combine the resulting low-OPT query with a weak-call update to prove strong learning under that added hypothesis.
ideas.title: Public Posterior-Tail Positive Theorem
ideas.why_promising: The residual obstructions identify the exact missing ingredient: posterior lower tails, not excess alone. This direction could produce a clean conditional positive result rather than another failed residual lemma.

ideas.risks: Finite explicit classes are validation-learnable, so the model must be framed as a black-box oracle/candidate-generation obstruction. Improper outputs may not fit a proper support-function abstraction.
ideas.summary: Formalize the fixed-slack learner as an additive support oracle with slack 2 beta and analyze adaptive query strategies geometrically. Start with two- and three-vertex examples showing target-bad faces remain legal under anchor/doping queries, then ask what cap-separation condition is sufficient when arbitrary improper legal outputs are allowed.
ideas.title: Support-Function Slack Oracle Game
ideas.why_promising: Anchor doping failures suggest a finite-dimensional obstruction that can be made precise. It may produce either a useful black-box lower bound or exact conditions under which support refinement is possible.

ideas.risks: Behavioral compression on observed unlabeled samples may not transfer to hidden-clean population accuracy. Stability assumptions may simply restate the missing regularity.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether sample splitting, unlabeled behavioral nets, canonical tie-breaking, or randomized hashing can transform an arbitrary efficient fixed-slack learner into a controlled-range or stable weak learner sufficient for DCHP. In parallel, build adversarial learners that defeat each proposed regularizer.
ideas.title: Canonicalization By Behavioral Nets
ideas.why_promising: If any weak regularization can be obtained generically, the DCHP route becomes much more plausible. If not, explorers can record precise obstructions instead of treating range control as a vague gap.
